question: How many jobs will the new Brevick Textiles factory create?

T.title: Textile factory to bring new jobs
T.text: The new Brevick Textiles factory will create 340 jobs when it opens on the edge of Saltmere, according to the company's announcement. Managing director Hilde Sorrel said positions would include machine operators, designers and warehouse staff, and that local applicants would be invited to open recruitment days. Production is expected to begin once the equipment is in place.

P.title: What the textile factory means for Saltmere
P.text: Brevick Textiles says its new factory near Saltmere will create 410 jobs once it opens. Human resources director Oskar Brandvik said roles would range from machine operators to designers and warehouse staff, and that recruitment days would be held for local applicants. Production is expected to begin after the equipment has been installed.

F1.title: College adds textile courses
F1.text: Saltmere College is adding short courses in textile machinery and pattern design, aiming to prepare residents for work in the region's growing clothing industry. Course leaders say places are open to adults returning to education as well as school leavers. Evening classes are available for those already in work.

F2.title: Traffic concerns near factory site
F2.text: Residents living near the planned factory site outside Saltmere have raised concerns about delivery lorries using narrow village roads. The residents' group has asked for a new access road and clear signage directing heavy vehicles away from the school and village centre. The group will present its concerns at the next parish meeting.
